# Manage the product roadmap

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

When multiple customer needs and product investments compete for delivery capacity. A prioritized outcome-based roadmap with explicit tradeoffs, accountable owners and a review cadence.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Collect and classify product evidence

agent-runnable


Consolidate customer problems, usage, support findings, technical risks and commercial commitments. Distinguish evidence from feature requests and identify which commitments already have contractual or launch constraints.

- Sources: [GitLab customer success management handbook](https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/customer-experience/csm/) · [NIST Secure Software Development Framework](https://csrc.nist.gov/Projects/ssdf)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Model options and dependencies

agent-runnable


For each candidate outcome, record the affected customers, expected value, engineering dependencies, operational cost and uncertainty. Identify research or security work that must precede a delivery commitment.

- Sources: [GitLab customer success management handbook](https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/customer-experience/csm/) · [NIST Secure Software Development Framework](https://csrc.nist.gov/Projects/ssdf)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Choose priorities and capacity allocations

human · human approval required


Product and engineering owners review tradeoffs with the relevant commercial and risk owners. Agree the outcomes to pursue and explicitly defer work that exceeds capacity instead of publishing every request as a promise.

- Sources: [GitLab customer success management handbook](https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/customer-experience/csm/) · [NIST Secure Software Development Framework](https://csrc.nist.gov/Projects/ssdf)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Translate priorities into owned delivery work

agent-runnable


Connect each selected outcome to an owner, success measure and the existing feature-delivery process. Record external communication commitments separately from internal target dates.

- Sources: [GitLab customer success management handbook](https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/customer-experience/csm/) · [NIST Secure Software Development Framework](https://csrc.nist.gov/Projects/ssdf)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Review results and revise the roadmap

human · human approval required


Compare shipped outcomes with customer evidence and actual cost. Update priorities and communicate approved changes to affected teams, retaining the reasoning behind major changes.

- Verify: A prioritized outcome-based roadmap with explicit tradeoffs, accountable owners and a review cadence.
- Sources: [GitLab customer success management handbook](https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/customer-experience/csm/) · [NIST Secure Software Development Framework](https://csrc.nist.gov/Projects/ssdf)
